# Ra.One
**Ra.One** is a 2011 Indian science fiction action film directed by Anubhav Sinha and starring Shah Rukh Khan and Arjun Rampal. The story centers on a video game created by Shekhar Subramaniam (Khan) and his son Prateek (Armaan Verma). The game features a protagonist named G.One and a powerful, self-learning artificial intelligence antagonist named Ra.One. When the game's mainframe fails, Ra.One breaches the digital barrier and enters the real world, seeking the player "Lucifer" (Prateek). He murders Shekhar's colleague Akashi and kills Shekhar upon discovering he is not Lucifer, prompting Prateek to bring G.One into the real world to fight him.
Throughout the film, Ra.One evolves from a digital construct into a living entity capable of shapeshifting, mind-reading, and creating copies of himself. G.One and Prateek eventually defeat Ra.One by exploiting a glitch in his programming, causing him to absorb his remains and return to the digital world. Months later, G.One is restored to the real world, where he protects his family. The film was notable for its extensive use of visual effects, which won the National Film Award for Best Special Effects, and for being one of the most expensive Bollywood productions at the time. It faced controversy regarding plagiarism allegations and hacking of its official website, but was a commercial success in India and gained international recognition.
